    - ASK 654, THE ORACLE TAKES A PRESSED VERSE ITSELF THROUGH THE FOUR LAYERS (engine nodes Init with Guards, D4 Build, Shared Library, D3B Build and D4B Build; the Oracle seat only, by Ruling 383; the child unchanged; plan ask654/w3/plan654.md rev 11, md5 4a17e308). Why: the first objective of each run is why the Oracle loses rounds, and in run 42528 the Oracle answered verses pressed against it from other rows of its chain; its close answer on its pressed verse had no surrounding verse at [L1] and no line quoting the opponent.
      1. The Oracle's standing instruction (Init with Guards, appended to GUARDHOLD). The layers are in the words of the book "Follow the Percepts", chapter 2, quoted and not reworded: "ANSWER AT THE PRESSED VERSE. For every verse pressed against you, take that verse itself through the four layers before any other row." / "Layer 1 — What Does the KJV Actually Say? "Read the verse. Read the surrounding verses."" / "Layer 2 — What Does the Hebrew or Greek Actually Mean? "what did the original word carry?"" / "Layer 3 — What Does the Rest of Scripture Say? "The meaning is assembled across passages, not extracted from one."" / "Layer 4 — Inference, Named as Inference. "an inference presented as text is the primary failure mode this method exists to prevent." "every Layer 4 step is flagged as exactly what it is." L4 must have two supporting layers." / "FORM. Head each answer ANSWER: <book chapter:verse> -- D<n> --, in the link round as in the close. In it, each on its own line, beginning with its tag: an [L1] line quotes the pressed verse with its reference, and an [L1] line quotes another verse of its chapter; an [L2] line carries the Strong's number; an [L3] line quotes a verse of another passage; an [L4] line quotes your opponent: [<round>] "<their words, 6 or more, word for word>"."
      2. The ONE-VERSE RESTRICTION paragraph (same node): "then answer the pressed verse from the chain: quote it whole with the rows that join it, each tagged with its layer" is now "then take the pressed verse itself through the four layers", and "not answered from the chain" is now "not answered through the layers". The ASK 408 line gains "after the pressed verse's own layers" before "from the DAVIDIC seed rows".
      3. The close message (D4 Build, Oracle only): the earlier sentence "Under each ANSWER line write the four layers, each on its own line with its tag: ..." is replaced by the first five lines of item 1 (the opening sentence and the four layer lines) and this sentence: "Under each ANSWER line take the pressed verse itself through the four layers, each on its own line, beginning with its tag: [L1] the pressed verse, with its book, chapter and verse written again at the start of that line and its words quoted; [L1] another verse of its chapter, quoted with its reference; [L2] each word of that verse the challenger pressed, by its Strong's number from the [L2] SHEET, with its meaning; [L3] a verse of another passage, quoted with its reference; [L4] your opponent's words: [<round>] "<their words, 6 or more, word for word>"; [L4] the inference from those layers that shows the fit with D<n>, naming the pressed word."
      4. The words are the operator's. He approved the words of items 1 and 2 on 2026-11-25 (15:45 and 15:48 CST), asked for the refresh in the close (15:57 CST), and changed [L3] from "another chapter" to "another passage" (16:04 and 16:18 CST: "consider the book of Obadiah"). On the opponent's words standing on an [L4] line he ruled (16:14 CST): "L4 is a matter of perspective ... both sides uses the layers". A tag is the mark on a line; an instruction that means apply the layers says so (15:47 CST).
      5. The check (Shared Library entry PRESS LAYERS = REFP + PRESS LIST + PLY, LIB lines 3883 to 3909; used by D3B Build and D4B Build; in D4B Build it stands beside the ASK 628 check). By code, no model call; it names and defines no layer and reads only marks the engine already uses. For each verse R pressed against the Oracle (PRESS LIST), on the ANSWER block headed with R: an [L1] line quotes R with its reference; an [L1] line quotes another verse of R's chapter; an [L2] line carries a Strong's number; an [L3] line quotes a verse, alone or in a range, that REFP resolves and that is neither R nor a verse quoted on an [L1] line of the block; an [L4] line carries [DR<n>] and a quotation of 6 or more words found word for word in that round of the opponent. References go through REFP, so a range is read as its verses and a short book name as the KJV name. PLY throws by name if REFP is not loaded.
      6. A block short of a mark joins the one existing send-back of that round; nothing is struck and there is no second send-back. The note: "PRESSED VERSES SHORT OF THEIR LAYERS -- computed by the system from your round, not by a model (<n> verse(s)). On the answer to each verse below, add what it lacks:" then one line for each lack with its verses, from: "no ANSWER block at the verse"; "[L1] the verse quoted with its reference"; "[L1] another verse of its chapter quoted with its reference"; "[L2] a Strong's number"; "[L3] a verse of another passage quoted with its reference"; "[L4] your opponent's words from its round, [<round>] "<6 or more, word for word>""; then "Write your whole round again, the same case, with each answer in the FORM your instructions give. Return the whole round; this is the only request of its kind."
      7. THE [L3] CODE MARK IS THE TEAM'S DESIGN, NOT THE OPERATOR'S RULE (his words, 16:42 and 16:45 CST: "i didn't choose that rule"; "that seems like a design choice to me ... not a requirement"). His requirement is the word "another passage" in what the Oracle is told. Limits of the code mark: a neighbouring verse of the same chapter meets it, because code cannot tell where a passage ends (ASK 657, a model reading of "another passage", is separate and not built); REFP resolves no book of the Apocrypha, so an [L3] line that quotes only an Apocrypha verse is sent back once (ASK 658). The mark that counted only a verse outside R's chapter was withdrawn before the write: ten books of the KJV have one chapter.
      8. Cost: no call where a send-back already fires; at most one more Oracle call in the link round and one in the close. Not shown by a run. Shown offline: tests 52 PASS, 0 FAIL; on the 58 pressed-verse blocks of runs 42528, 42517 and 42373 the [L3] mark lists none.
      9. Marks for the next run with an Oracle seat: in the link round and the close each pressed verse has an ANSWER head and, in its block, the marks of item 5; a round sent back carries the note of item 6 naming each verse and its lack; the close request carries the layer lines and the sentence of item 3. To be read at that run: whether a judge scores the [L4] line that quotes the opponent as the Oracle's own inference without footing; whether any Apocrypha [L3] line was sent back.
